name: Atmospheric CO₂
summary: CO₂ 427.3 ppm, up 2.12 ppm on a year
state: Mauna Loa recorded 427.3 ppm in the week of 25 Oct, 2.12 ppm higher than a year earlier, inside the 2–3 ppm/yr Watch band (NOAA GML). Strong El Niño years usually speed up CO₂ growth as land carbon sinks weaken.
for_you: No direct action needed. Faster CO₂ growth means more warming locked in.

sources.title: NOAA GML — Mauna Loa CO₂ trends

why: CO₂ concentration is the main long-run driver of warming; the growth rate shows whether emissions cuts are biting.
drivers: Fossil emissions, land sinks, El Niño (weakens sinks), wildfires.
